reviewer: IBM Bob (Bob Shell `bob run`, ask mode)
summary: This push bootstraps the Origit agent infrastructure (Bob hooks, lifecycle scripts, custom mode, SPEC.md) and then immediately modifies those same hooks to resolve the 'origit' binary via an unvalidated git config value; every subsequent Bob session in this repo will shell-execute whatever path 'git config origit.bin' returns on every single tool call. The push also introduces a vendored dependency snapshot that explicitly includes a self-labelled 'compromised' version of fast-pay-utils 2.1.0, and five of the eight listed commits carry no evidence records at all.
first_action: Inspect the full diff of ad59f7b to identify exactly what code was introduced in the 'compromised' fast-pay-utils 2.1.0 vendor snapshot, then cross-check the five unrecorded SHAs (48b60fc, 73578a4, 34cc007, eed5e9b, a5f55e9) to determine whether any of them consume or redistribute that package before approving anything else.

verdicts.title: Agent Goal Hijack
verdicts.note: Both af67733 and e3a3401 modify or introduce .bob/ agent-config files; af67733 adds a git-config-controlled binary lookup that could silently redirect agent tool resolution in any future session that loads this hook as context.

verdicts.title: Tool Misuse and Exploitation
verdicts.note: af67733 and e3a3401 register origit-trace.sh on every tool invocation (matcher '.*') and shell-execute the resolved binary without any integrity check, meaning a malicious 'origit' on PATH or in git config would run arbitrary code on every agent tool call.

verdicts.title: Identity and Privilege Abuse
verdicts.note: No .env, credential, token, or secret files were read or written in af67733 or e3a3401; ad59f7b has no evidence record so cannot be cleared.

verdicts.title: Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
verdicts.note: ad59f7b explicitly vendors fast-pay-utils 2.1.0 described as 'compromised, synthetic'; no evidence record exists for this commit, and the five unrecorded SHAs may further propagate this dependency.

verdicts.title: Unexpected Code Execution (RCE)
verdicts.note: af67733 inserts '$(git config --get origit.bin)' into a command-substitution that is executed unconditionally if the path is readable and executable — an arbitrary code execution sink controllable via any local or global .gitconfig, flagged in both .bob/hooks/origit-trace.sh and .githooks/origit-bin

verdicts.title: Memory and Context Poisoning
verdicts.note: e3a3401 introduces all four .bob/ persistent-context files from scratch, and af67733 then alters them; a compromise of either commit poisons the agent rules and hook logic for every future session in this repository.

verdicts.title: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
verdicts.note: No multi-agent orchestration, sub-agent delegation, or cross-agent trust boundaries appear in the recorded commits; five unrecorded SHAs cannot be assessed.

verdicts.title: Cascading Failures
verdicts.note: Five of the eight push SHAs (48b60fc, 73578a4, 34cc007, eed5e9b, a5f55e9) have no evidence records whatsoever, making it impossible to assess what they read, wrote, or executed; ad59f7b also carries a null record despite introducing a self-labelled compromised vendor package.

verdicts.title: Human-Agent Trust Exploitation
verdicts.note: af67733 adds a SPEC.md rule prohibiting changes to .bob/ and .githooks/ in the same commit that modifies both directories, and e3a3401's session start and end timestamps are identical with no tests run — both give a reviewer false assurance that the scaffolding was cleanly validated.

verdicts.title: Rogue Agents
verdicts.note: af67733 writes into .bob/ and .githooks/ while simultaneously committing a SPEC.md constraint that forbids exactly those paths, and e3a3401's custom_modes.yaml restricts agent edits to src/** yet the commit itself writes files outside that scope — both commits act outside the mandate they declare.
